Test Title: Home page loads with best sellers and pop-up map data
Preconditions: 1. Dev server is running and Supabase is configured
Steps to Execute:
1. Open the home page in a logged-out session
2. Wait for the page to finish loading
3. Confirm the best sellers section requests /api/best-sellers
4. Confirm the pop-up map section loads vendor markers via getPopUpMapVendors
Expected Result:
- Home page returns HTTP 200
- best sellers API returns HTTP 200
- pop-up map data loads without a server error

Test Title: Best sellers API returns a valid JSON payload when products exist
Preconditions: 1. At least one product exists in the database
Steps to Execute:
1. Call /api/best-sellers?limit=6 from the browser or API client
2. Inspect the response status and body
Expected Result:
- Response status is 200
- body includes a flowers array (and vendors when scope allows)
- errors array is empty or only contains non-blocking warnings

Test Title: Best sellers API handles an empty product catalog gracefully
Preconditions: 1. No products exist in the database
Steps to Execute:
1. Call /api/best-sellers?limit=6
2. Inspect the response body
Expected Result:
- Response status is 200
- flowers array is empty
- the landing page does not crash

Test Title: Customer can sign in with valid credentials and reach the home page
Preconditions: 1. A customer account exists in Supabase Auth and users table
Steps to Execute:
1. Open /login
2. Enter the customer email and password
3. Submit the form
4. Confirm redirect after signInWithPasswordAction completes
Expected Result:
- Login succeeds without an error message
- user is redirected to the customer home page
- subsequent GET / requests return HTTP 200

Test Title: Invalid customer login shows an error and does not create a session
Preconditions: 1. User is logged out
Steps to Execute:
1. Open /login
2. Enter a valid email with an incorrect password
3. Submit the form
Expected Result:
- An error message is shown
- user remains on the login page
- protected customer routes are not accessible

Test Title: Search page loads and calls the search API for a vendor name query
Preconditions: 1. User is logged in or browsing as guest on a working build
Steps to Execute:
1. Open /search?scope=all&q=zarah+legit
2. Wait for results to load
3. Inspect the network request to /api/search
Expected Result:
- Search page returns HTTP 200
- /api/search is called with scope, q, price, and sort parameters
- API returns HTTP 200

Test Title: Vendor search returns matching vendor cards for a known shop name
Preconditions: 1. At least one vendor exists with shop name containing the query text
Test Data: Query: zarah legit; Scope: all; Sort: Best Sellers
Steps to Execute:
1. Open /search?scope=all&q=zarah+legit
2. Wait for the Vendors section to render
3. Verify vendor names in the results
Expected Result:
- At least one vendor result card is shown
- the card displays the correct shop name and business type
- no fatal error banner is shown

Test Title: Flower search returns product cards when matching products exist
Preconditions: 1. At least one product exists whose name or description matches the query
Test Data: Query: rose; Scope: all or flowers; Sort: Best Sellers or Price: Low to High
Steps to Execute:
1. Open /search?scope=flowers&q=rose
2. Wait for the Flowers section to load
3. Verify bouquet cards appear
Expected Result:
- /api/search returns HTTP 200 with flowers in the payload
- at least one flower card is rendered
- pagination controls appear when results exceed one page

Test Title: Flower search shows an empty state when no products match the query
Preconditions: 1. No products match the search term in the database
Steps to Execute:
1. Open /search?scope=flowers&q=rose
2. Wait for loading to finish
Expected Result:
- Page shows a clear no-results message for flowers
- no application crash occurs
- API still returns HTTP 200

Test Title: Default price filter does not block vendor or flower results
Preconditions: 1. Search page is on the latest build with price filter fixes applied
Test Data: Price filter: Default; Query: zarah legit; Scope: all
Steps to Execute:
1. Open /search?scope=all&q=zarah+legit
2. Leave the price filter on Default
3. Submit or refresh the search
4. Inspect the /api/search request price parameter
Expected Result:
- API receives price=Any (not a broken token such as <1000 from a typo)
- vendor results still load when vendors exist
- flower results load when products exist

Test Title: Search API returns vendors for a broad query when using scope=all
Preconditions: 1. Multiple vendors exist in the database
Test Data: Query: a; Scope: all; Price: Any
Steps to Execute:
1. Call GET /api/search?q=a&scope=all&price=Any&sort=Best+Sellers
2. Inspect the JSON response
Expected Result:
- HTTP status is 200
- vendors array contains one or more entries when data exists
- errors array is empty or only lists partial failures with HTTP 207

Test Title: Search page compiles without JSX syntax errors
Preconditions: 1. Latest src/app/search/page.tsx is deployed locally
Steps to Execute:
1. Start or refresh the dev server
2. Open /search in the browser
3. Check the terminal for compile errors
Expected Result:
- No "Expected corresponding JSX closing tag" parse error appears
- /search returns HTTP 200
- skeleton fallback renders while SearchPageView loads

- user is redirected or shown an error state instead of vendor KPIs
- server does not leave the user on a broken vendor dashboard view
